message.content: The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria). This ancestor was a small, insect‑eating mammal that lived roughly 100–110 million years ago during the Paleocene epoch.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. The lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) are both mammals, but they belong to different orders: lions are Carnivora, zebras are Perissodactyla. Their common ancestor would be at the level of the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, or maybe earlier. But we can give a more precise answer: The last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria). That ancestor lived around 100 million years ago. So the answer: the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, likely a small, insectivorous mammal from the Paleocene.

We should provide a concise answer. No tool needed.
